intent_snapshot.goal: A Claude MCP server whose own bundle changed on disk after it started reports itself as stale with an explicit reconnect action instead of refusing with run_entry_required, and a Lane-mode batch start is refused when the coordinator's loaded plugin build differs from the workspace plugin build (Spec branch-boundary D3, D4).

acceptance.assertion: After the server's own bundle file changes on disk following startup, a tools/call for enroll, start_unattended_batch, retire_stale_batch, advance_assurance or submit_review is refused with reason_code plugin_bundle_stale and a recovery_action naming a reconnect of the immune-brain MCP server, before any phase admission is consumed and with no Kernel mutation; with the bundle unchanged the same calls behave as before; status still answers and carries a stale warning; an unreadable bundle file at check time refuses with the same reason code.
With a stale bundle and no admission for the call, the refusal is plugin_bundle_stale rather than run_entry_required; with a current bundle and no admission it is still run_entry_required.

A Lane-mode batch start in the plugin's own source repository is refused with batch_runtime_contract_mismatch, naming both plugin paths and a reload action, when the loaded plugin build differs from the workspace plugin build; it starts as before when the loaded plugin is the workspace plugin or an identical build; a serial batch start is unaffected.

attestations.summary: Provenance checks out: df497490's only parent is 3fa20fcc and its tree is 54a31a27. In callTool, the bundle staleness check runs before any session read, phase admission or Kernel call, and status still answers with a warning. The Lane-mode skew refusal runs only on a new Lane start, and the regenerated dist bundle matches the source. Tests cover AC1, AC2 and AC3, including the negative cases.

advisory_findings.summary: watchBundleIdentity re-hashes the bundle only when its size or mtime changes. A rewrite that keeps both the same is not detected, and the server keeps acting as if the bundle were current.

evidence.trigger: The bundle is replaced in place with different bytes of the same size, and its mtime is preserved (for example a copy that keeps timestamps) → stale() returns false, and authority calls run on the old bundle without a plugin_bundle_stale refusal

advisory_findings.summary: The stale-bundle refusal covers every tool except status, not just the five named in AC1. That is safe (it fails closed), but tools like repair_authority_state now also refuse until the server is reconnected.

evidence.trigger: The bundle changed after startup, then any tool other than status is called, for example repair_authority_state → it is refused with plugin_bundle_stale even though AC1 does not name that tool
